title: Joseph Smith’s Revelations, Doctrine and Covenants 106
book: Joseph Smith's Revelations: A D&C Study Companion from the Joseph Smith Papers

footnotes.text: Warren Cowdery, Freedom, NY, to Oliver Cowdery, Kirtland, OH, 14 Jan. 1834, inThe Evening and the Morning Star,Jan. 1834, 127.

At some point after recording the revelation in Revelation Book 2, Oliver Cowdery supplied “Cowdery” as Warren’s last name. (Revelation, 25 Nov. 1834, in Revelation Book 2, p. 116, inJSP,MRB:649 [D&C 106:1].)

Freedom appears to have been a central location for several branches in western New York. In January and April 1835, conferences were held there, attended by representatives from areas such as Westfield, Chautauque County; Portage, Allegany County; Kortright, Delaware County; and Avon, Livingston County. (“A Summary,”Messenger and Advocate,Feb. 1835, 1:75; Minutes,Messenger and Advocate,Apr. 1835, 1:101–102.)
See Luke 10:7; Revelation, Sept. 1830–F [D&C 31:5],herein; and Revelation, 22–23 Sept. 1832 [D&C 84:79],herein.
See James 5:8; Revelation, 3 Nov. 1831 [D&C 133:17],herein; and New Testament Revision 2, p. 149 (second numbering) [Joseph Smith Translation, Revelation 1:3].
See 1 Thessalonians 5:2; and New Testament Revision 2, p. 77 (second numbering) [Joseph Smith Translation, Luke 12:44].
See Revelation, 7 Aug. 1831 [D&C 59:2],herein; and Revelation, 15 Mar. 1832 [D&C 81:6],herein.

Pratt,Autobiography,121. A letter from Oliver Cowdery to Warren dated 29 April 1834 indicated that Warren was still not a member of the church at that time. (Oliver Cowdery, Kirtland Mills, OH, to Warren Cowdery, [Freedom, NY], 29 Apr. 1834, in Cowdery, Letterbook, 40–41.)

“A Summary,”Messenger and Advocate,Dec. 1834, 1:45. The issue contains the notice of the death of a nine-year-old in Kirtland on 12 December 1834, meaning it was published sometime after 12 December. (Obituary for Cornelius Camfield,Messenger and Advocate,Dec. 1834, 1:41.)
